segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Section 1: Week 52 Listening: Annual Review and Next Steps

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: Hi, Daniel. Thanks for coming in. So, this is your annual review for the community learning centre. How do you feel the year went?

segments.speaker: Daniel
segments.text: Hi, Mia. Honestly, it was a busy year. I think I improved a lot in teaching, but I also made some mistakes.

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: That's normal. Let's look at the four areas: teaching, admin, teamwork, and professional development. First, teaching. You taught three evening classes this year. How did they go?

segments.speaker: Daniel
segments.text: The evening classes went well. Attendance was good, and most students passed their final test. But I think my instructions were sometimes too long.

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: Yes, I noticed that too. Short instructions are better. Now, admin. You were responsible for the weekly attendance records. Did you finish them on time?

segments.speaker: Daniel
segments.text: Not always. I was late with the records twice, in March and May. I'm sorry about that.

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: Okay, that's noted. For next year, we can set a reminder. Now, teamwork. You worked with two other teachers on the summer project. How was that?

segments.speaker: Daniel
segments.text: The summer project was great. We shared lesson plans, and I learned a lot from the others. But I sometimes didn't reply to emails quickly.

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: Right. Quick replies help the team. Finally, professional development. You attended two workshops this year. Which ones?

segments.speaker: Daniel
segments.text: I went to a workshop on classroom management and one on using videos in class. The classroom management one was very useful.

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: Good. So, overall, your teaching is strong, but you need to improve admin and email communication. For next year, I suggest you make a short checklist before each class. Also, try to reply to emails within one day.

segments.speaker: Daniel
segments.text: That sounds practical. Can I also get feedback from a senior teacher?

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: Yes, we can arrange that. I'll send you a form to fill in. And remember, the deadline for the next year's plan is June 30th.

segments.speaker: Daniel
segments.text: June 30th. Got it. Thank you, Mia.

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: You're welcome. Let's meet again in September to review your progress.

segments.speaker: Daniel
segments.text: Sounds good. I'll start working on the checklist right away.

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: Great. Also, don't forget to submit your self-assessment form by the end of this week.

segments.speaker: Daniel
segments.text: Okay, I'll do that. Thanks for the reminder.

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: You're welcome. See you in September.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Section 2: Year-End Review and Next Steps

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Good morning, everyone. This is a simulated announcement for our community learning centre. I’m going to talk about the year-end review and what comes next. Please listen carefully and take notes if you like.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: First, the year-end review will take place on December 15th. It will start at 9 a.m. and finish at 11 a.m. The review will be held in Room 204, not in the main hall as in previous years. Please arrive ten minutes early to sign in.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Second, there are four things we will check during the review. These are: your attendance record, your completed assignments, your progress test scores, and your speaking participation. Each area is important, but the speaking participation is often the one people forget. Make sure you have evidence of your speaking practice, such as a short recording or a signed log.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Third, after the review, you will receive a short report. The report will show your strengths and the areas you need to improve. You will get this report by email within one week after the review. If you do not receive it, please contact the office.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Fourth, we will offer a follow-up planning session on January 10th. This session is optional but strongly recommended. In the session, you can discuss your goals for the next term and choose new courses. The session will be online, and you will receive a link by email.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Now, let me give you some advice for the review. Many students make the same grammar mistakes again and again. For example, they forget to use the past tense when talking about last year, or they use 'he' instead of 'she' when referring to a female teacher. To help you, we have prepared a short checklist. The checklist has five points. You can download it from our website. Use it to check your own writing before the review.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: The five points on the checklist are: 1) Check past tense verbs. 2) Check subject-verb agreement. 3) Check articles (a, an, the). 4) Check prepositions (in, on, at). 5) Check pronoun use (he, she, it, they). These are the most common errors we see.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Finally, remember that the review is not a test. It is a chance to see your progress and plan your next steps. If you have questions, please email the office. Thank you for listening.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Section 3: Week 52 Listening Part 3: Final Review and Action Plan

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.text: Good morning, Mia and Leo. This is our last tutorial before the exam. Let's review your progress and make a short checklist for the final week. Mia, can you start with the grammar points that still cause problems?

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: Sure. I still make mistakes with subject-verb agreement, especially when the subject is far from the verb. For example, I wrote 'The list of items are on the desk' instead of 'is'. Also, I sometimes forget to use the past perfect when talking about two past events. Like 'When I arrived, the film started' instead of 'had started'.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.text: Good. Those are common. Leo, what about you?

segments.speaker: LEO
segments.text: I have trouble with articles. I often say 'I need advice' but then I say 'an advice' by mistake. And I mix up 'few' and 'a few'. Also, I sometimes use 'although' and 'but' together, which is wrong.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.text: Right. So for the checklist, let's focus on three areas: subject-verb agreement, past perfect, and articles. Also, avoid double conjunctions. Now, let's talk about your listening and reading strategies. Mia, how do you handle multiple-choice questions?

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: I read the options first, then listen for keywords. But I sometimes choose an option that is mentioned but not correct.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.text: That's a classic distractor. You need to listen for the whole meaning, not just words. Leo, what about matching headings in reading?

segments.speaker: LEO
segments.text: I read the headings first, then skim the paragraphs. But I often spend too much time on one paragraph.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.text: Set a time limit. Now, let's plan the final week. I suggest you do one full practice test on Monday, then review your mistakes on Tuesday. On Wednesday, focus on grammar exercises. Thursday, practice speaking with a partner. Friday, review vocabulary. Saturday, rest. Sunday, light review. Any questions?

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: What about writing task 2? Should we practice more essays?

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.text: Yes, write at least two essays and get feedback. Also, check your use of linking words. Leo, you mentioned you sometimes overuse 'moreover'. Try to vary your connectors.

segments.speaker: LEO
segments.text: Okay. And for listening, should we listen to podcasts?

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.text: Yes, but choose ones with transcripts so you can check your understanding. Also, practice note-taking. Now, let's make the checklist. Mia, you write it down. Include: check subject-verb agreement, use past perfect for earlier past, check articles before nouns, avoid double conjunctions, read options carefully, manage time in reading, write two essays, vary linking words, listen with transcripts, and rest on Saturday.

segments.speaker: Mia
segments.text: Got it. I'll share it with Leo.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.text: Good. Remember, the exam is on Monday next week. Good luck!

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Section 4: Week 52 Listening Part 4: Final Review and Action Plan

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Good morning, everyone. I hope you are all feeling focused and ready for the last stretch of the term. Today I want to talk about the final review for your academic writing course. This is our last session, so I will focus on the four areas you need to check before the exam. I will also give you a short action plan for the remaining week, so you know exactly what to do each day.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: First, let's look at the four areas. The first area is grammar. Many of you still make the same mistakes. For example, you often forget the third-person -s, as in 'she write' instead of 'she writes'. You also confuse 'since' and 'for'. Remember, 'since' is used with a point in time, like 'since 2020', and 'for' is used with a period, like 'for three years'. Another common error is the misuse of articles. You say 'I am student' instead of 'I am a student'. These errors are small, but they affect your score.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: The second area is vocabulary. You need to use academic words correctly. Don't just memorize long words; learn how to use them in sentences. For instance, 'analyze' is a verb, and 'analysis' is a noun. You should also avoid repeating the same words. Try to use synonyms, but make sure they fit the context.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: The third area is structure. Your essays need a clear introduction, body paragraphs, and conclusion. Each paragraph should have one main idea. Use linking words like 'however', 'therefore', and 'in addition' to connect your ideas. But don't overuse them.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: The fourth area is task response. Make sure you answer the question fully. If the question asks for your opinion, give it clearly and support it with reasons. Don't just describe the topic.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Now, let me give you a short action plan for the final week. On Monday, review your grammar notes and do the exercises on pages 45 to 50. On Tuesday, practice vocabulary from the academic word list. On Wednesday, write a full essay under timed conditions. On Thursday, review your essay and check for the four areas. On Friday, take a rest and do light review. On Saturday, do a final mock test. And on Sunday, relax and prepare your materials for the exam.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Remember, the exam is on Monday next week. Good luck with your preparation.
